open_points.subject: Function sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input”, while A03 rule 1 gives it a writable exchange directory and rule 4 permits opening paths inside both that directory and the read-only runtime.
open_points.question: May function code read runtime files or create/read arbitrary files in the exchange directory, or must filesystem access be limited to the files representing its declared inputs and outputs?
options: Permit all access inside the exchange directory and runtime
Permit only declared input/output files
Expose no filesystem API to function code
open_points.default_guess: Permit only declared input/output files in the exchange directory and deny user-code access to other runtime paths.

open_points.subject: Function determinism and absence of clock/randomness
open_points.text: A03 claims functions have no clock or randomness and requires identical output digests, but its closed trap list omits nondeterministic standard-library and runtime facilities such as other clock APIs, process/runtime observations, thread scheduling and cryptographic randomness exposed outside the named modules.
open_points.question: What complete enforceable boundary makes execution deterministic, and what is the required outcome when code uses an unlisted nondeterministic facility?
options: Broaden syscall/runtime isolation to enforce determinism
Expand the closed trap list to every permitted facility
Drop the guarantee and treat repeatability as unverified
open_points.default_guess: Enforce a syscall-level allowlist and classify any disallowed observation as sandbox_violation.

open_points.subject: Sandbox resource-limit outcome classification
open_points.text: A03 rule 5 says “a limit hit” takes precedence and yields resource_exhausted, but does not define how a memory, process-count or scratch limit is recognized when Python catches the resulting exception or the operating system reports it as an ordinary failure.
open_points.question: What observable evidence constitutes each limit being hit, including when user code catches the error, and how is it distinguished from crashed?
options: Externally monitor and record every limit event
Classify specified OS signals and error codes as limit hits
Classify only directly measured limits as resource_exhausted
open_points.default_guess: Use external accounting or kernel-enforced events and let a recorded limit event win even if the code catches an exception.

open_points.subject: Authored TrialCase input and expected-output shape
open_points.text: A04 rule 1 requires that input values and expected outputs “fit” the contract ports, but does not say whether every input must be present, whether extra names are refused, or whether a present expected_outputs must contain every output port rather than a subset.
open_points.question: What exact key set is required for trial inputs and for a present expected_outputs object?
options: Require exact input and output port sets
Require exact inputs but allow partial expected outputs
Allow partial inputs and outputs
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly every input port and, when expected_outputs is present, exactly every output port, with no extra names.

open_points.subject: TrialExecution failure details
open_points.text: A03 rule 6 says the kernel keeps bounded exception type and message as failure_detail, and A07 rule 5 defines disclosure of a TrialExecution failure_detail, but M07 TrialExecution has no failure_detail field.
open_points.question: Do trial executions persist a failure detail, and if so what field and disclosure rules apply?
options: Add bounded failure_detail to TrialExecution
Discard all trial failure detail
Store failure detail in a separate trace record
open_points.default_guess: Add the same bounded failure_detail field and disclosure treatment used for NodeExecution.

open_points.subject: Flow node identifiers and flow endpoints
open_points.text: A05 rule 2 represents a flow input or output endpoint with the empty string for ordering, but no rule forbids a FlowNode whose node_id is the empty string or explains how an edge structurally distinguishes that node from a flow endpoint.
open_points.question: Are empty node identifiers forbidden, or are flow endpoints represented by a separate tagged form?
options: Forbid empty node_id
Use tagged node and flow endpoint variants
Allow empty node_id with another discriminator
open_points.default_guess: Forbid an empty node_id and represent flow endpoints explicitly in the edge model.

open_points.subject: Mapped value-output aggregation limits
open_points.text: A13 rule 6 creates one StoredValue containing all mapped value results, while A15 rule 4 says an oversized node-produced value concludes “the element” contract_violation; a mapped node has no aggregate NodeExecution and its last element may already have succeeded.
open_points.question: What happens when individually valid mapped results form an aggregate array larger than stored_value_bytes_max, and which NodeExecution records that failure?
options: Fail the last element and replace its result
Write a separate mapped-node aggregate record
Prevent mapping when the aggregate cannot fit
Fail the run without a NodeExecution
open_points.default_guess: Write an explicit aggregate failure record for the mapped node and discard the aggregate value.

open_points.subject: Element conclusion across multiple attempts
open_points.text: A13 rule 7 says an element’s conclusion is “its NodeExecution’s status”, but an element can have several NodeExecutions after service_unreachable, not_sent, unknown resolution and resend; it does not identify which record controls the current conclusion.
open_points.question: How is the current conclusion derived from an element’s ordered sequence of attempts and resolutions?
options: Use the highest attempt_number only
Fold all attempts with an explicit state-transition table
Let any failed historical attempt permanently fail the element
open_points.default_guess: Use the highest attempt number, interpreting an outcome_unknown record together with its EffectAttempt resolution.

open_points.subject: Manifest structural validation
open_points.text: A08 rule 5 handles absent or invalid JSON and selected missing fields, but later rules assume capabilities, instances, exposed_as, required_headers, paths and idempotency_key have particular JSON types and shapes without defining refusals for other valid-JSON shapes.
open_points.question: What complete manifest schema is validated, in what order, and how are malformed-but-valid-JSON field types classified?
options: Define a complete manifest schema and ordered validation
Treat every unlisted shape as manifest mismatch with one generic reason
Permit coercion of compatible shapes
open_points.default_guess: Define a complete strict schema and classify the first schema violation as manifest mismatch.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision lookup
open_points.text: M28 and A08 require reading `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` “at the configured manifest_revision”, but do not define how a revision is resolved, checked out, verified or associated with the bytes read.
open_points.question: What exact mechanism maps manifest_location plus manifest_revision to immutable file bytes?
options: Read through a version-control repository API
Require manifest_location to be an immutable revision directory
Ignore revision and read the working tree
open_points.default_guess: Require manifest_location to resolve to an immutable directory whose revision is verified at startup.

open_points.subject: Per-service credentials
open_points.text: A17 rule 1 says the configuration holds “per service, the selected manifest instance name and one credential”, while rule 2 explicitly defines behavior for “a service the installation gives no credential”.
open_points.question: May a configured service omit a credential, and if so is omission accepted at startup or refused only when an invocation is built?
options: Credential is optional and invocation fails pre-send
Every selected service must have a credential at startup
Manifest declares whether a credential is required
open_points.default_guess: Allow omission at startup and produce credential_unresolved only when that service is invoked.

open_points.subject: Credential file decoding
open_points.text: A17 rule 2 refuses a secret file whose value is empty or contains a control character, but does not define the file encoding, whether a final newline is stripped, or what happens for invalid UTF-8.
open_points.question: How are credential-file bytes converted to an HTTP header value?
options: Require exact nonempty UTF-8 with no trimming
Strip one line ending then validate UTF-8
Treat the secret as opaque header bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require UTF-8, strip one conventional trailing line ending, then reject empty values, controls and invalid header characters.

open_points.subject: Service base URL validity and joining
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute http or https URL with a host, while A09 forms the target by removing a trailing slash and appending the operation path; userinfo, query, fragment, unusual base paths and multiple trailing slashes are not addressed.
open_points.question: Which URL components and canonical forms are allowed in api_base_url, and what exact joining rule applies?
options: Allow only scheme, host, optional port and normalized base path
Allow all absolute URLs with standards-based resolution
Treat the base URL as literal text and append the path
open_points.default_guess: Reject userinfo, query and fragment, normalize only the explicitly permitted trailing slash, and append to a validated base path.

open_points.subject: Path-placeholder port cardinality
open_points.text: A09 rule 2 requires a placeholder’s schema type to be string or integer but does not require its port cardinality to be one; a many port always supplies a list and therefore can never be placed in the path.
open_points.question: Must every input used by a path placeholder have cardinality one at binding proposal time?
options: Require cardinality one
Use one placeholder segment per list element
Allow the proposal and fail each send
open_points.default_guess: Require cardinality one and refuse the binding proposal otherwise.

open_points.subject: Port names used in multipart headers
open_points.text: A09 constructs `Content-Disposition` parameters directly from port names, including `name="<port>"` and `filename="<port>"`, but no rule constrains or escapes quotes, backslashes, control characters or non-ASCII characters in port names.
open_points.question: What port-name grammar or escaping algorithm makes multipart headers unambiguous and injection-safe?
options: Restrict all port names to a safe identifier grammar
Apply a specified multipart quoted-string encoding
Use RFC 5987 extended parameters
open_points.default_guess: Restrict port names to a conservative ASCII identifier grammar when contracts and bindings are issued.

open_points.subject: Media-type syntax and comparison
open_points.text: A02 requires a media type on file ports, A05 compares media types for equality, and A09 compares a response on type and subtype while ignoring parameters, but no rule defines valid media-type syntax, case normalization or whether declared parameters are allowed.
open_points.question: What media types may be declared, how are they canonicalized, and what equality rule is used by proofs and HTTP validation?
options: Require lowercase bare type/subtype
Allow parameters with a canonical parser
Treat declarations as opaque strings except for HTTP responses
open_points.default_guess: Require a valid bare type/subtype, canonicalize it to lowercase, and use that canonical value everywhere.

open_points.subject: Credentials in service error bodies and diagnostics
open_points.text: A17 says a credential never enters a failure detail, log line or response, while A09 rule 7 stores an excerpt of an untrusted error body as failure_detail; a service can echo the credential or an HTTP client exception can include request headers.
open_points.question: How must credentials be prevented from entering error excerpts, exceptions and logs?
options: Redact exact resolved credential values before persistence or logging
Never retain service error bodies or transport exception text
Rely on services and HTTP libraries not to echo credentials
open_points.default_guess: Never log request headers and redact exact credential values from every diagnostic before it crosses the invoker boundary.

open_points.subject: Personal data in approval request previews
open_points.text: M24 and A10 say an approval preview includes the built request, including URL, query and JSON body, while A07 says an agent reading an approval receives personal data only as digest and class. Personal-data inputs can be embedded directly in that request representation.
open_points.question: What redacted representation of a built request is returned to an agent so that personal data cannot leak indirectly through its URL, query, body or multipart description?
options: Redact every request component derived from personal data
Return only request_digest and structural metadata to agents
Forbid agents from inspecting approvals containing personal data
open_points.default_guess: Return the request digest and a structural request description with every personal-data-derived component replaced by digest and class.

open_points.subject: HTTP failure-detail text encoding
open_points.text: A09 retains bytes from an arbitrary error response as failure_detail, M23 models failure_detail as bounded text, and A20 truncates it at a UTF-8 character boundary, but an error body need not be valid UTF-8.
open_points.question: How are arbitrary response bytes decoded and truncated into failure_detail?
options: Require valid UTF-8 or omit the detail
Decode UTF-8 with replacement
Store a bounded base64 or hexadecimal representation
open_points.default_guess: Decode as UTF-8 with replacement and truncate the resulting text at a character boundary.

open_points.subject: List continuation-token scope
open_points.text: A16 rule 6 defines a continuation token only as the store position of the last item and rejects one naming no position, but does not bind it to the list operation, filters, actor or disclosure view that created it.
open_points.question: Can a continuation token from one list or query be reused for another, and what request facts must the token authenticate?
options: Bind it to operation, filters and actor/view
Bind it only to the list kind and filters
Allow any existing store position in any list
open_points.default_guess: Bind the token to the list operation, normalized filters and caller disclosure view, in addition to the store position.

open_points.subject: Token-list reread recovery
open_points.text: A16 rule 2 says an invalid reread discards the old list and refuses every request until a reread passes, but does not say whether the failed file hash becomes the “last read” hash or how a later restoration to identical earlier bytes triggers another parse.
open_points.question: What state and hash are retained after a failed configuration reread, and exactly when is the file retried?
options: Retry reading and parsing on every request while invalid
Store the invalid hash and retry only after bytes change
Keep the last valid hash but separately force retries
open_points.default_guess: Enter an invalid-configuration state and retry the full read and validation on every request until it succeeds.

open_points.subject: Release dependency closure
open_points.text: A20 says a release pins the exact versions of every kernel dependency and sandbox runtime, but release v1 specifies only “CPython 3.12” and no patch version, dependency list, versions or bubblewrap version.
open_points.question: What exact runtime, bubblewrap and kernel dependency versions constitute release v1?
options: List and hash every artifact in the design
Define a checked-in lockfile and runtime image as normative release data
Leave exact versions to the implementation build
open_points.default_guess: Make a checked-in lockfile plus hashed CPython runtime and bubblewrap build the normative release-v1 dependency set.
